newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares up at noon on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares up at noon on technical rebound.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were slightly up at midday on Monday on a technical rebound after last Friday's sharp falls, but trading was sluggish with most investors sidelined waiting for a clearer direction, brokers said.
The B index inched up 0.135 points or 0.16 percent to 84.573 points on volume of 4.415 million shares worth $3.461 million.
Trading was focussed on market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development, which was supported by institutions despite selling pressure from retail investors, brokers said.
"A wait-and-see mood dominated the market though some institutions were seen pulling the index up by support buying in selective stocks, especially Lujiazui," one broker said.
"With the thin trading volume, the market will test the low levels again in the short term," another broker said. "But the index is likely to see support at the 75-point level."
Of 43 B shares, 36 traded, with 20 up, four flat and 12 down.
Shanghai Material Trading Centre 900927.SS was the star on speculative buying, jumping $0.014 or 7.95 percent to $0.190 on volume of 10,000 shares.
Shanghai Automation Instrument followed on a technical rebound, rising $0.010 or 4.90 percent to $0.214 on volume of 83,800 shares.
The market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui was the most actively traded on heavy selling despite institutional support, shedding $0.006 or 0.42 percent to $1.390 on volume of 1.2 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index rose also on a technical rebound, but market sentiment was cautious after Friday's plunges, brokers said.
The index rose 16.186 points or 1.18 percent to 1,392.096 on volume of 290.0 million shares worth 3.7 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index put on 74.203 points or 1.96 percent to 3,860.789 points.
Newcomer Zhejiang Guyuelongshan Shaoxing Wine was the star on expectations of good earnings, soaring 2.06 yuan or 7.92 percent to 28.06 yuan on volume of 4.4 million shares.
